title: Convergence soak + burst trace harness for Dedicated autoscale stability
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a reusable harness that runs mixed steady-state and burst traffic patterns against Dedicated GPU pools to validate autoscaler convergence, steady-state throughput, and p95 latency stability over multi-day soaks. The harness should produce traceable artifacts (time-series tokens/sec, p95, p99, fail-rate) and a regression detector that alerts on statistical shifts in latency tails or throughput dropouts.
motivation: We occasionally see long-tail regressions after kernel or batching changes that only show up after hours of mixed load. Current soak runs are ad-hoc and focused on throughput rather than end-to-end latency tails and scale-in/scale-out convergence. This ticket builds a declarative harness to reproduce, detect, and triage those regressions for Dedicated capacity customers.
test_plan: Implement traffic generator scenarios: steady-state (tokens/sec plateau), periodic small bursts (1-5s every 30s), sustained burst windows (10-15m), and back-to-back step increases to exercise scale-up and scale-down logic.
Support multi-tenant mixes: high-throughput short seq vs low-throughput long-seq workers; ensure KV cache warmup behavior included.
Run runs for 48-72 hours for soak validation and for 2-4 hour quick smoke runs in CI mode.

Capture metrics at 10s granularity: tokens/sec, request/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, autoscaler decisions (add/remove), and scaling cooldown timestamps.
Export traces and envelopes compatible with Console dashboards and the regression detection pipeline (CSV/time-series + raw request samples for flagged windows).
metrics_to_track: p95_latency_ms and p99_latency_ms (per model and per route)
scale_up_time_seconds and scale_down_time_seconds (from policy trigger to capacity available)
convergence_delta (time to reach within X% of target throughput after step-up)
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run in 'ci-quick' mode (2h) and 'soak' mode (>=48h) and emit artifacts to S3 and Console-compatible location.
Regression detector flags true positive p95 shifts >= 20% with false positive rate < 5% on synthetic control runs.
Observed convergence time for step-up scenarios documented and repeatable; engineers can reproduce within +/- 15% of baseline across repeated runs.
Artifacts include a time-aligned CSV of tokens/sec, p95, autoscaler events, and at least one raw request sample per flagged window for debugging.
Runbook section added describing triage steps when detector fires (links to relevant dashboards and recommended first checks).
notes: Initial prototype run (2026-03-08) showed intermittent p95 spikes correlating with KV cache evictions during long bursts — need to capture per-request cache hit metadata.
Discussed alert thresholds with SRE and PM; agreed on progressive alerting: CI-mode warnings for minor shifts, pager for regressions that persist > 30m.
Follow-up task: add network throttling variant to simulate noisy neighbors (split into sub-issue if validated as a cause).
Plan to integrate this harness into nightly regression suite once false-positive tuning is complete.
